harmonicFunction: E (I) - Luminous, triumphant tonic reinforced by ringing open B and high E strings
Aadd9 (IVadd9) - Subdominant chord enriched with the 9th (B) providing spacious harmonic shimmer
F#7add11 (II7add11) - Secondary dominant with open string extensions providing forward harmonic pull
Bsus4 (Vsus4) - Suspended dominant resolving cleanly into the E major tonic

techniques.name: Asymmetric Meter Shifts & Whammy Bar Expressive Phrasing
techniques.description: Mastering the seamless transition between 7/4, 3/4, and 4/4 time signatures while picking wide-interval open string extensions, followed by lyrical whammy bar articulation in the solo

notes: Open string voicings: Keep the open B and high E strings ringing freely across all chord shapes
7/4 counting: Counted as a bar of 4/4 followed by a bar of 3/4 (1-2-3-4, 1-2-3)
Whammy bar articulation: Depress the tremolo arm slightly before picking and release it to pitch, creating a vocal sigh
sequence: Memorize the signature chord voicings with ringing top strings (Aadd9, F#7add11, Bsus4)
Count the intro time signature shifts out loud with a metronome at 132 BPM
Practice alternate picking through the arpeggiated figures to ensure clean string separation
Incorporate subtle Floyd Rose / synchronized tremolo dips to shape notes in the solo
tips: Use your thumb over the top of the neck to fret bass notes while freeing lower fingers for chord extensions
Do not mute the open top two strings—they are the sonic glue that ties the entire song together
Apply an analog delay set to approximately 350ms to recreate the spacious studio aura of Le Studio

effects.delay: Stereo tape delay set to 350ms on the solo

beginner.title: Chord Voicings & Drone Strings
steps: Learn the fingerings for Aadd9, F#7add11, and Bsus4
Ensure the high B and E strings ring cleanly without fret buzz or finger muting
Practice strumming the basic verse progression in standard 4/4 time

intermediate.title: Asymmetric Counting & Intro Riff
steps: Count the 7/4 and 3/4 meter shifts smoothly with a metronome
Alternate pick through the arpeggiated intro pattern at 110 BPM before pushing to 132 BPM
Lock into Neil Peart's drum accents and Geddy Lee's driving bass line

advanced.title: Whammy Bar Solo Articulation & Nuance
steps: Learn Alex Lifeson's solo phrasing, paying close attention to micro-tonal pitch bends
Use the whammy bar to scoop into notes and create smooth, vocal vibrato
Balance pick dynamics and delay trails to allow sustained notes to bloom naturally

commonMistakes: Muting the open B or high E strings while fretting complex chord shapes
Losing count during the transition from 7/4 into 3/4 and 4/4
Using excessive whammy bar dips that knock the guitar out of tune instead of subtle musical vibrato
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: Open-string chord fingering clarity and arpeggiation drills
15 minutes: Metronome practice in 7/4 time (divided 4+3) at 100-132 BPM
15 minutes: Whammy bar scoop and pitch-matching drills over the solo backing track
focusAreas: Whammy bar pitch control and vibrato width
metronomeWork: Count 7/4 as 1-2-3-4 followed by 1-2-3 with accents on beat 1 and beat 5 at 120 BPM
